To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AcrAB efflux pump in E. coli is a broad substrate pump that exports biocides such chlorhexidine and triclosan as well as multiple classes of antibiotics.
the multiple antibiotic resistance locus and regulon in Escheichia coli and the multiple drug resistance efflux pumps in P. aeruginosa are important mechanisms of antibiotic and biocide resistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of resistance of microorganisms to antibiotics and biocidal agents.
the mechanisms by which bacteria resist the effects of antimicrobial agents.
the molecular mechanisms of drug resistance in bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
active efflux is a common mechanism for resistance to biocides and antibiotics and is a significant factor in the development of drug resistance in bacteria.
the prudent use of antibiotics will guard against the development of drug-resistant mutants, and preserve the efficacy and effectiveness of these valuable agents.
the use of antimicrobials in the environment is a risk factor for the development of antimicrobial resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

biocides and antibiotics can select for the expression of multidrug effl ux pumps in bacteria, that such pumps can be activated by mutations in regulatory genes and that the mar regulon is a paradigm for such a response.
we have demonstrated that the efflux pumps of P. aeruginosa and the MarR regulon in E. coli can export both biocides and antibiotics, and that the MarR regulons are inducible by biocides.
we have shown that the mar regulon is a paradigm for an inducible, multiple drug resistance locus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prudent use of antibiotics will help preserve their efficacy.
the use of biocides and antibiotics must be carefully controlled and judiciously applied to minimize the selection of drug resistance in the environment and in the clinic.
biocide and antibiotic resistant bacteria share a common resistance mechanism.
